page: Microsoft Azure F4als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz with a 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The underlying processor includes AVX-512 vector extensions, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration instructions like VAES and SHA-NI. The instance contains no GPU accelerators and includes no local ephemeral storage, requiring remote or premium disk volumes for persistent storage.

Performance benchmarks highlight significant single-threaded compute strength. In stress-ng single-core tests as well as single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, the server ranks within the top tier. Multi-core performance registers in the middle tier, yielding 15,088.73 on stress-ng and 13,471.73 on PassMark CPU tests. Memory throughput reaches 53.17 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 34.25 GB/sec for writes. The hardware executes static web serving at 10.9 GB/sec and handles small language model text generation at a strong 333.29 tokens per second, though prompt processing for medium models drops to the bottom tier due to the four-core profile.

The primary operational tradeoff of the F4als_v7 is its compact 8.0 GB memory envelope and lack of local storage, which confines its cost efficiency to workloads requiring high-clock dedicated execution rather than in-memory dataset handling. This hardware profile provides a cost-effective alternative for tasks that demand raw processing speed without the overhead of surplus RAM. The configuration is suitable for CI/CD compilation runners, CPU-bound batch tasks, web serving, and single-threaded compute jobs.
